section_summary: This final section concerns Japanese textile production, export allocations, pricing, and sales after the war. Much of the correspondence addresses proposed cotton textile sales to Siam, including credit terms, rice and tin exports, and barter. Other documents cover the Textile Mission report, scientific exchange about rayon research, and plans for distributing 1947 exports.

subfiles.title: War Department textile questions and replies
subfiles.about: The message exchanges plans for singlets, linen, textile finishing, and raw silk sales.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo reports revised singlet supply estimates and seeks guidance on linen prices, finishing cotton goods, and silk sales. Washington discusses selling gray goods, allocating finishing capacity, and a forthcoming raw silk auction.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Cooper Tire request
subfiles.about: The note asks for a response to Cooper Tire's request for a Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Requests that Cooper Tire be informed about future report distribution.

subfiles.title: Cooper Tire request for Textile Mission report
subfiles.about: Cooper Tire requests two copies of the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Schaefer requests duplicate copies, citing the company's use of cotton and rayon.

subfiles.title: Reply to Cooper Tire
subfiles.about: Whitman says copies are unavailable but promises two when the printed report is ready.
subfiles.summary: Places Schaefer on the list for two copies.

subfiles.title: Cotton textile contract negotiations
subfiles.about: USCC requests a date for final textile selections needed to conclude contracts.
subfiles.summary: Reports talks with prospective buyers and asks when final country selections can occur.

subfiles.title: British calculation of Japanese textile consumption
subfiles.about: The British Embassy explains its proposed annual ceiling for Japanese textile consumption.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum details a proposed ration, estimates consumption by fibre, and suggests a 160,000-ton annual ceiling while leaving allocation within that ceiling to occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on textile consumption ceiling
subfiles.about: The Department objects to a binding maximum for Japan's textile consumption.
subfiles.summary: The Department maintains its objection to a fixed ceiling binding SCAP, while acknowledging the British calculations and considering alternative policy language.

subfiles.title: USCC request for approval of Siam textile sale
subfiles.about: Henderson seeks State Department approval for a credit sale of Japanese textiles to Siam.
subfiles.summary: Requests approval and views on financing larger future sales.

subfiles.title: Attached joint letter concerning Siam textile sale
subfiles.about: The largely unreadable attachment appears to concern approval of the Siam textile transaction.
subfiles.summary: Attachment text is largely absent from the OCR.

subfiles.title: Rayon microscopy and scientific exchange
subfiles.about: Rose seeks approval to send rayon microscopy photographs and research material to Professor Horio.
subfiles.summary: Describes Horio's rayon research and asks the Department to forward photographs and a letter through SCAP.

subfiles.title: Clayton endorsement to Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Clayton endorses the proposed Siam textile sale and its short-term credit.
subfiles.summary: Argues textiles would encourage Siamese rice deliveries and that expected export proceeds support repayment.

subfiles.title: Clayton reply to Henderson
subfiles.about: Clayton supports the immediate Siam sale but reserves judgment on further textile requirements.
subfiles.summary: The Department supports the proposed credit transaction because textiles could stimulate rice exports and Siam appears able to repay. It cannot yet assess additional purchases. Clayton encloses his endorsements to the War and Agriculture Secretaries.

subfiles.title: Clayton endorsement to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Clayton urges approval of the proposed sale of 30 million yards of textiles to Siam.
subfiles.summary: He presents textiles as an inducement to increase rice shipments and argues that Siam can repay the proposed $4 million credit over six months. Page 548 contains a rewritten version or fragment of the same letter.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Bangkok about Siamese dollar commitments
subfiles.about: The Department seeks information on Siam's ability to meet the textile sale's cash payment.
subfiles.summary: Requests urgent details on dollar exchange commitments to private importers.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on textile quality and prices
subfiles.about: Cole addresses British concerns about prices for older Japanese textile stocks.
subfiles.summary: Says USCC and SCAP accept quality adjustments in principle but find none warranted for current stocks.

subfiles.title: British objection to pricing older textile stocks
subfiles.about: Percival asks for lower prices on older Japanese textiles of allegedly inferior quality.
subfiles.summary: He distinguishes acceptance of a general price basis from the need to adjust prices for older mixed-cotton stocks. He asks how buyer governments can justify equal prices for goods of differing quality.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning textile sales
subfiles.about: The damaged telegram appears to discuss USCC sales of exportable textiles.
subfiles.summary: Most substantive wording is unreadable in the OCR.

subfiles.title: American Viscose follow-up on Horio materials
subfiles.about: Morton acknowledges report copies and asks whether Rose's earlier scientific packet arrived.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Martin for fifteen report copies and requests confirmation of receipt of photographs and journals.

subfiles.title: Reply to American Viscose
subfiles.about: A mostly unreadable reply follows Morton's inquiry about the scientific packet.
subfiles.summary: The OCR preserves little beyond the closing and file reference.

subfiles.title: Bangkok report on Siamese textile purchase
subfiles.about: Siam confirms urgent interest in 30 million yards but cannot yet calculate import commitments.
subfiles.summary: Promises further figures once available.

subfiles.title: Siamese Textile Mission request for dollar credit
subfiles.from: Atcheson, Tokyo, relaying Siamese Textile Mission
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Siamese Legation, Washington
subfiles.about: The mission requests $1,500 for expenses that cannot be paid with released yen.
subfiles.summary: Seeks dollar credit for military lodging and return flights.

subfiles.title: Rose letter on printed Textile Mission report
subfiles.about: Rose praises the printed report and asks whether all mission members received copies.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a circulation letter and asks about copies for foreign members.

subfiles.title: Notice of Textile Mission report availability
subfiles.about: Rose announces the report's printed edition and its importance to understanding Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that the report is available from the Government Printing Office for fifteen cents.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning report distribution
subfiles.about: A largely unreadable reply concerns Rose's November 27 letter.
subfiles.summary: Only the file reference and drafting notation remain legible.

subfiles.title: USCC acknowledgment of Siam sale endorsements
subfiles.about: Henderson thanks Clayton and awaits formal War and Agriculture concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Notes that both departments must concur before USCC can sell on credit.

subfiles.title: British follow-up on textile quality
subfiles.about: Percival requests an urgent answer on the quality and pricing of older Japanese textile stocks.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether old stocks match current American goods or are being priced alike regardless of quality.

subfiles.title: Paris request for Textile Mission report
subfiles.from: A. P. Muelberger, U.S. Embassy Paris
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Muelberger requests two report copies for a French wool industry organization.
subfiles.summary: Asks that copies be sent by air pouch.

subfiles.title: Report copies sent to Paris
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Paris
subfiles.about: The Department sends two public copies of the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Fulfills Muelberger's request and notes that more copies are available.

subfiles.title: Bangkok telegram on financing Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Moffat reports Siam's difficulty making the proposed cash payment and explores alternatives.
subfiles.summary: Seeks an advance against tin, while reporting Siamese questions about yen payment and commodity barter.

subfiles.title: Forwarding of rayon research materials
subfiles.about: The Department forwards letters, microscope photographs, and journals concerning Professor Horio.
subfiles.summary: Encloses scientific materials for transmission in Japan.

subfiles.title: Certified copy note
subfiles.about: A filing note certifies a copy of a signed original.
subfiles.summary: Marked as a true copy of the signed original.

subfiles.title: Authority to sign textile contracts
subfiles.about: USCC asks the Department to verify foreign representatives' authority to bind their governments.
subfiles.summary: Gardiner seeks government statements identifying authorized signatories for textile sale contracts. The attached list names prospective buyer countries and territories.

subfiles.title: Bangkok telegram on Siamese payment alternatives
subfiles.about: Siam proposes long-term credit, barter, or a combination for the textile purchase.
subfiles.summary: Stanton reiterates USCC's shorter credit offer and points to a tin sale as a source of dollars. He forwards the proposed barter terms, including glutinous rice that might be exported to Korea.

subfiles.title: Combined Textile Committee on 1947 exports
subfiles.about: The committee revises expected textile availability and proposes a successor process for 1947 allocations.
subfiles.summary: It estimates fewer than 50 million additional fourth-quarter yards and suggests including them in first-quarter 1947 supply. As it is closing, it proposes that future distribution plans go to the Inter-Allied Trade Board.

subfiles.title: Whitman reply on textile allocations
subfiles.about: Whitman responds to the proposal for submitting 1947 textile allocations to the trade board.
subfiles.summary: Says interested parties will be consulted before a proposal is submitted.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on proposed letter
subfiles.about: An internal note discusses a proposed letter and advance review of its wording.
subfiles.summary: Much of the handwritten text is unreadable.

subfiles.title: USCC letter on country access to textile sales
subfiles.about: Gardiner asks State to confirm sales policy and forward-sale arrangements for Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: He seeks confirmation that USCC may sell beyond priority countries after offering them goods, and that forward sales remain acceptable. He notes a proposed January 13 deadline for trade-board members to state quantities they will buy.

subfiles.title: Reply file copy concerning Gardiner letter
subfiles.about: A nearly unreadable reply or file copy follows Gardiner's December 30 letter.
subfiles.summary: Only the recipient and file reference are discernible.
